title: A river between the stores
body:
25 July 1511. The Portuguese took the bridge today and withdrew to their ships at dusk. The market in Upeh is on one bank; the royal stores and the mosque are on the other. Even now no carter will promise to get a load across before morning.

Your clerk has counted the last sacks at the landing. The royal storekeeper asks you to put them aside for the court. On the Upeh steps a woman holds out her empty rice measure.

choices.label: Offer the sacks for sale in Upeh
choices.outcome_text: Upeh has rice tonight without needing the crossing. The royal storekeeper strikes the expected sacks from his tally.

choices.label: Keep the sacks in reserve for the royal store
choices.outcome_text: The storekeeper counts the sacks for the court. None of this lot reaches the Upeh steps tonight.

notes: fact: The bridge joined the commercial north bank and the royal south bank. Portuguese troops took it on 25 July and withdrew to their ships at dusk (docs/research/1511-events.md §1, Phase IV).
gameplay: The carter, the tally and the distribution choice are fictional ways to show the interruption to trade.
